name: Close and fund private investments
summary: After a private investment is approved and its documents are negotiated, investment counsel and a paralegal run the closing: subscription agreements, tax and KYC forms for fund commitments, or funds flow, conditions and consents for direct and co-investments. Two officers sign for the model manager as agent for each owning client account, private markets operations sets up the commitment or holding split across those accounts, verifies the wire instructions by call-back and pays from several client accounts with dual approval. Closings slow down when the fund administrator returns the subscription package, when a competition filing is needed, and when sponsors set closing dates at short notice that strain same-day funding and approvals.

baseline.org_archetype: A provincial not-for-profit asset manager of about $79 billion that closes about 35 direct and co-investment transactions and 15 fund commitments a year, held mainly in segregated client accounts.
baseline.notes: Documents exchanged by email and the document system, electronic signatures common from 2020, set-up keyed into the private markets system and payments released in the custodian portal.

unit_of_work: one closing (direct deal or fund commitment)
trigger: Investment counsel receives a committee-approved deal or fund commitment with negotiated execution versions, or a committee decision on a sponsor-led co-investment whose documents are largely fixed.
end_state: The investment is closed and funded or the subscription accepted, the commitment or holding is set up and split across client accounts, and the closing set and key terms are filed; or the closing is abandoned.

volume.seasonality: More closings in the fourth quarter as sponsors push to close before year end.

evidence.note: 35 direct and co-investment transactions in 2021 (mgr_nr21) plus about 15 fund commitments a year (organisation file, tier C) give about 4 a month, matching the process map range.

FTE from about 11 hours of counsel time per closing at 4.5 closings a month, plus closing work that the step times do not split out. Loaded cost from the organisation file, above the Job Bank median for NOC 41101 ($69.74 an hour in Toronto, 2023-2024) because investment counsel at large Canadian funds are senior hires.
About 10 hours a closing for checklists, subscription and KYC packages, signature pages and the closing set; loaded cost from the organisation file.
About 5 hours a closing for set-up in the private markets system, wire verification, payment instructions and confirmation; loaded cost from the organisation file.
Independent checks and payment approvals; loaded cost from the organisation file.
Funds flow and ownership split for private equity co-investments and direct deals (about 45% of direct closings).
Funds flow and ownership split for infrastructure and credit direct closings (about 25% of direct closings).
Funds flow, adjustments and ownership split for real estate closings (about 30% of direct closings).

Organisation file role not listed on this process; updates the restricted or watch list for direct deals.
Organisation file role not listed on this process; signs execution documents as an authorised officer with a second signatory.

systems.name: Document management system and virtual data rooms
Email, video calls and collaboration suite
Private markets investment accounting and monitoring system (commitments, calls, distributions, valuations)
Custodian portal (custody, accounting records, net asset value reports, cash and corporate action notices)
Code of conduct, personal trading pre-clearance and attestation system
Electronic trading and broker platforms (equity, bond and FX multi-dealer)

steps.name: Open the closing matter and confirm the approval scope
steps.description: Investment counsel receives the committee decision and the negotiated documents, reads the approval conditions, the approved amount and how it is split across the owning client accounts, opens a closing matter in the document system and names the deal team, operations and outside counsel contacts.

evidence.note: Approval by the Management Investment Committee or an Investment Department Committee within thresholds precedes every closing; matter set-up is common practice. Times tier C.

steps.name: Build the closing checklist and signing plan
steps.description: The paralegal builds the closing checklist from the agreement: deliverables, conditions, consents, signatories for the model manager as agent for each owning client account, tax and KYC forms and the funding timetable, and circulates it to the deal team, operations and outside counsel.

error.defect_description: A signatory, client account or deliverable is missed from the checklist.

next.condition: private equity co-investment or direct deal
infrastructure or private credit direct closing

evidence.note: Checklist practice is standard; the split of closings (30% fund subscriptions, 70% direct and co-investments split 45/25/30 by asset class) rests on about 15 fund commitments and 35 direct and co-investment transactions a year in the organisation file and mgr_nr21.

steps.name: Complete the subscription agreement and investor questionnaire
steps.description: For a fund commitment the paralegal completes the general partner's subscription agreement and investor questionnaire for each owning client account: legal name, investor category, regulatory and public body status, bank details, notice contacts and the committed amount, checking the answers against prior subscriptions.

error.defect_description: Wrong investor category, entity name or bank detail for one of the client accounts.

evidence.note: No industry standard subscription form; branching questionnaires; times tier C.

steps.name: Prepare tax forms and self-certifications
steps.description: The tax analyst completes the tax forms the fund asks for, such as Form W-8BEN-E for United States funds and residency self-certifications, for each client entity, confirms the treaty or exemption position the client relies on and returns signed forms to the paralegal.

error.defect_description: Wrong chapter 4 status or treaty claim on a form.

evidence.note: W-8BEN-E documents a foreign entity's withholding and FATCA status; treaty positions of Canadian pension and public bodies are common practice. Times tier C.

steps.name: Assemble the KYC and anti-money-laundering package
steps.description: The paralegal gathers what the fund administrator needs to identify the investor: constating documents and statutory basis of each client body, incumbency and signing authority certificates, the investment management agreement extract appointing the model manager and lists of directors, and sends the draft package for pre-review.

error.defect_description: Stale certificate or missing beneficial ownership statement.

evidence.note: Collating investor KYC materials is labour intensive; times tier C.

steps.name: Fund administrator pre-reviews the subscription package
steps.description: The general partner's counsel or fund administrator checks the draft subscription agreement, questionnaire, tax forms and KYC documents against its own requirements and either clears them or returns a list of deficiencies, usually by email.

evidence.note: Several rounds of email are usual before the subscription is final; the 28% return rate and two to ten day turnaround are tier C.

steps.name: Correct subscription deficiencies
steps.description: The paralegal fixes the items the administrator raised, obtains corrected certificates or forms from the tax team or the client's corporate secretary, and resends the corrected pages with a covering note listing each change.

evidence.note: Rework rounds are described in the source; times tier C.

steps.name: Check the funds flow and ownership split (private equity)
steps.description: The private equity associate reviews the draft funds flow memo from the sponsor's or buyer's counsel for co-investments alongside a lead sponsor: purchase price, adjustments, fees and expenses, the amount payable by each owning client account and holding entity, and the currency, and reconciles it to the approved amount and split.

error.defect_description: Amount by client account does not match the approved split or currency.

evidence.note: Buyer's counsel drafts the funds flow about a week before closing and it is locked one to three business days before; times and the wait for the sponsor's draft are tier C.

steps.name: Check the funds flow and ownership split (infrastructure or private credit)
steps.description: The infrastructure or private credit associate reviews the draft funds flow memo from the sponsor's or buyer's counsel for direct infrastructure and credit deals: purchase price, adjustments, fees and expenses, the amount payable by each owning client account and holding entity, and the currency, and reconciles it to the approved amount and split.

error.defect_description: Amount by client account does not match the approved split or currency.

evidence.note: Buyer's counsel drafts the funds flow about a week before closing and it is locked one to three business days before; times and the wait for the sponsor's draft are tier C.

steps.name: Check the funds flow and ownership split (real estate)
steps.description: The real estate associate reviews the draft funds flow memo from the sponsor's or buyer's counsel for property acquisitions and joint ventures: purchase price, adjustments, fees and expenses, the amount payable by each owning client account and holding entity, and the currency, and reconciles it to the approved amount and split.

error.defect_description: Amount by client account does not match the approved split or currency.

evidence.note: Buyer's counsel drafts the funds flow about a week before closing and it is locked one to three business days before; times and the wait for the sponsor's draft are tier C.

steps.name: Track closing conditions and deliverables
steps.description: Investment counsel works through the closing checklist with outside counsel: conditions precedent, third-party consents, officer certificates, resolutions of holding entities, and any regulatory notification, and decides whether a filing must be made before closing.

next.condition: competition or foreign investment filing needed before closing
deal terminated or allocation withdrawn by the sponsor

evidence.note: Filing thresholds ($400 million parties, $93 million target) mean only larger control deals file; the 12% share and 3% termination rate are tier C.

steps.name: Prepare and file regulatory notifications
steps.description: With outside counsel, investment counsel prepares the Competition Act pre-merger notification or Investment Canada Act filing, or a request for an advance ruling certificate, collects the client and the model manager information the forms need and coordinates filing with the other parties.

control.basis: Competition Act (Canada) Part IX pre-merger notification and Investment Canada Act

evidence.note: Notification, advance ruling certificate and Investment Canada Act routes; times tier C.

steps.name: Wait for clearances and third-party consents
steps.description: The deal waits for the statutory waiting period to expire or for an advance ruling certificate, and for consents from lenders, landlords or co-owners; outside counsel answers any information request from the regulator.

next.condition: clearance or consent refused or deal walks away

evidence.note: 30-day waiting period, advance ruling certificates in 14 to 21 days, Investment Canada Act review up to 45 days extendable by 30; the 14 to 60 day range adds consents and is tier C.

steps.name: Update the restricted or watch list
steps.description: The compliance analyst adds the target, its listed affiliates or the sponsor's listed holdings to the restricted or watch list in the code of conduct system for the period around signing and closing, and records who on the deal team holds confidential information.

control.basis: Securities Act (Ontario) prohibition on trading or tipping with undisclosed material information, applied through the code of conduct restricted list

evidence.note: Restricted lists around private deals are common practice at Canadian pension managers to prevent trading on confidential information; times tier C.

steps.name: Check final documents against the approval
steps.description: Investment counsel compares the execution versions, funds flow and subscription pages with the committee approval: amount, client account split, structure and any approval conditions, and confirms every checklist item is ready. A material change in terms goes back for re-approval.

control.basis: The model manager Investment Approval Policy and committee delegated authorities: execution must stay within the approved terms

next.condition: material change in price, structure or split

evidence.note: Approval authorities between the Board, the Management Investment Committee and department committees are defined; the 4% re-approval rate is tier C.

steps.name: Committee re-approves changed terms
steps.description: The deal team circulates a short update paper to the committee that approved the deal, chaired or co-chaired by the chief investment officer, which approves the changed price, structure or split by email or at a special meeting, or withdraws approval.

control.basis: The model manager Investment Approval Policy: re-approval of material changes to approved terms

evidence.note: Management Investment Committee co-chaired by the CIO and CRO; re-approval by circulation is common practice; times tier C.

steps.name: Authorised officers sign the execution documents
steps.description: Two authorised signing officers, usually the general counsel with a senior investment officer, sign the agreements, subscription pages and certificates for the model manager as agent for each owning client account, often electronically; signature pages are held in escrow until closing.
outputs: signed signature pages held in escrow

control.basis: The model manager signing authority policy: two authorised signatories for investment agreements made as agent for clients

evidence.note: Signature pages held until release at closing are standard closing mechanics; the two-signatory rule is an assumption from common signing authority policies.

steps.name: Set up the commitment or holding in the private markets system
steps.description: The private markets operations analyst creates the fund commitment or direct holding in the private markets system: legal entity, currency, commitment or cost amount, split across owning client accounts, fee terms, reporting contacts and investor portal access, and requests custodian set-up of the new asset.

error.defect_description: Wrong client split, currency or commitment amount keyed.

evidence.note: Data from subscription documents is re-keyed into the investor's and sponsor's systems; times tier C.

steps.name: Independently check the set-up
steps.description: The manager of private markets operations compares the system record with the signed documents, approval and funds flow, ticks the set-up checklist and either releases it or sends it back for correction.

control.basis: Maker-checker review of new investment records before payments or valuations use them

next.condition: fund commitment with no payment at closing

evidence.note: Four-eyes review of static data is common practice; the 17% share of fund closings without a payment (first capital call follows later) and 8% correction rate are tier C.

steps.name: Obtain and verify the wire instructions
steps.description: The analyst takes the payee's wire instructions from the funds flow or closing notice and compares them with instructions received earlier, then calls a known contact at the sponsor, seller's counsel or administrator on a number already on file to confirm them.

control.basis: Call-back verification of new or changed payment instructions

evidence.note: Verify payment details through a second channel; call back on an independently obtained number. Rates tier C.

steps.name: Escalate and re-verify suspicious instructions
steps.description: The manager escalates instructions that changed late or could not be confirmed, calls the counterparty's finance lead and the deal counsel independently, obtains signed confirmation and records the outcome before any payment is set up.

control.basis: Call-back verification of new or changed payment instructions

evidence.note: Business email compromise targets changed payment details; times tier C.

steps.name: Arrange funding and foreign exchange for the client accounts
steps.description: The cash and collateral analyst checks that each owning client account will hold enough cash in the right currency on the closing date, books foreign exchange or raises cash from money market holdings, and confirms the funding to private markets operations.
inputs: closing amounts by account and currency

error.defect_description: Funding booked late or in the wrong currency.

evidence.note: Most private closings are in US dollars and are paid from several client accounts; short notice strains same-day funding as the process map notes. Times tier C.

steps.name: Create the payment instructions
steps.description: The analyst keys one payment instruction per owning client account in the custodian portal with the verified beneficiary details, amount, currency and value date, attaching the funds flow and approval as support.

error.defect_description: Amount or value date keyed wrongly.

evidence.note: Re-keying from the funds flow into the custodian portal is manual in the period; times tier C.

steps.name: Approve the payment instructions
steps.description: The manager of private markets operations compares each instruction with the funds flow, approval and verified instructions and releases it in the custodian portal as second approver; payments above the senior threshold also need the vice president.

control.basis: Dual authorisation of payments in the custodian portal under the model manager's payment authority matrix

evidence.note: Two approvers above a set amount is standard practice; the 60% share above the threshold reflects closing sizes of tens to hundreds of millions and is tier C.

steps.name: Senior approval of a large closing payment
steps.description: The vice president of investment operations reviews the payment against the approval and funds flow and gives the senior release required for large amounts, usually the day before closing.

control.basis: Payment authority matrix: senior approval above a threshold

evidence.note: Senior approval thresholds are common in payment authority matrices; the model manager's threshold is not public.

steps.name: Hold payments and release them on the closing date
steps.description: The custodian holds the approved payments until the value date and sends the wires on the closing morning, while counsel runs the closing call and releases signature pages once receipt of funds is confirmed.

evidence.note: Documents are released only after receipt of funds is confirmed; the hold until the closing date is tier C.

steps.name: General partner accepts the subscription at its closing date
steps.description: For fund commitments without a payment at closing, the general partner countersigns and accepts the subscription at the fund's next closing date and sends a welcome letter and portal access; the first capital call follows later.

evidence.note: General partners hold periodic closings; the one to three week wait is tier C.

steps.name: Confirm the closing and record the funded amounts
steps.description: The analyst confirms the wires settled or the subscription was accepted, records the funded or committed amount by client account in the private markets system and notifies the deal team, valuations, accounting and the cash team.

evidence.note: Post-closing confirmation and notification are common practice; the 20% announced share is tier C, based on the model manager releasing selected transactions.

steps.name: Clear the announcement and pass it to communications
steps.description: Investment counsel agrees with the counterparty what can be disclosed about the transaction, checks the deal facts and approved wording with the deal team, and sends the cleared facts to corporate communications for a news release.

control.basis: Confidentiality clauses of the transaction documents and the model manager disclosure practice

evidence.note: The model manager names selected transactions publicly; clearance with counterparties under confidentiality terms is common practice. Times tier C.

steps.name: Compile the closing set and record key terms
steps.description: The paralegal collects the signed documents, certificates and wire confirmations into the closing set in the document system, records reporting, consent and fee obligations in the term tracker and sends the commitment record to capital calls, asset monitoring and valuations.

error.defect_description: Key obligation missed from the term tracker.

next.condition: closing set filed and handed over

evidence.note: Closing sets are often finished days or weeks after closing; times tier C.

exceptions.name: Subscription package returned by the administrator
exceptions.description: About 28% of fund subscription packages come back with deficiencies (wrong investor category, stale certificates, tax form errors) and go through another round.

exceptions.name: Competition or foreign investment filing
exceptions.description: Control acquisitions above the thresholds need a Competition Act notification or Investment Canada Act filing and wait 30 to 60 days for clearance and consents.

exceptions.name: Changed or unconfirmed wire instructions
exceptions.description: Late changes to payee details are escalated and re-verified by call-back before any payment.

exceptions.name: Terms changed beyond the approval
exceptions.description: Price, structure or client split moves outside the approval and the committee re-approves or withdraws.

exceptions.name: Closing abandoned
exceptions.description: The sponsor cuts back or withdraws the co-investment allocation, the deal terminates, or a clearance or re-approval fails.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from receipt of the approved, negotiated documents to closing set filed
benchmarks.population: Closings of fund commitments and mid-market co-investments by a Canadian public asset manager

evidence.note: Author's estimate: funds flow drafted about a week before closing (dealroom_ff), 30 to 45 day regulatory waits on the minority of deals that file (osler_comp); very large deals take months (bcg_close) but most of the model manager's closings are minority co-investments and fund subscriptions.

benchmarks.unit: new deals in 2021 plus two follow-ons

benchmarks.population: Complaints to the FBI Internet Crime Complaint Center

pain_points.description: Sponsors set closing dates at short notice, so funding, foreign exchange and senior approvals are squeezed into the last day or two.

evidence.note: Stated in the organisation file's process description; author's reading.

pain_points.description: Each sponsor has its own subscription form and KYC list, so packages are filled by hand for each client account and often come back for corrections.
The same commitment data is keyed into the subscription pages, the private markets system and the custodian portal, with checks at each step.

evidence.note: Re-keying described for sponsors; the investor side is the author's reading.

pain_points.description: Payment fraud through changed wire instructions is a standing risk at every closing.

sources.title: The model manager posts 2021 net return of 9.6%, outperforms benchmark (news release, 25 April 2022)
sources.publisher: The model manager via Cision Newswire
sources.supports: 35 direct and co-investment transactions in 2021; private equity made four new fund commitments totalling $1.5 billion; named commitments of US$500 million and US$325 million; $79 billion of assets.

sources.title: The model manager 2021 Annual Report
sources.supports: Investment Approval Policy sets board approval of material investment decisions; the Management Investment Committee (CIO and CRO co-chairs, with the General Counsel) recommends every decision needing board approval and delegates to three Investment Department Committees with thresholds, with Legal represented; private equity closed $2.3 billion of transactions in 2021 including eight new co-investments or direct deals and two follow-on investments.

sources.title: ILPA issues model subscription agreement for private equity funds
sources.supports: ILPA released a model subscription agreement because fund closing was a priority for improvement; each manager recreated the core agreement for each fund; standard language reduces review time and legal cost for both parties.

sources.title: The use of online subscription agreements in private markets (Travers Smith briefing)
sources.supports: Subscription agreements collect bank details, regulatory status and investor assurances through branching questionnaires; there is no industry standard form; finalising and signing usually takes several rounds of email with the sponsor or its lawyers; collating investor KYC materials is labour intensive; the sponsor re-keys the data into its systems; manual collation risks error.

sources.title: About Form W-8 BEN-E
sources.supports: Foreign entities use Form W-8BEN-E to document their status for chapter 3 and chapter 4 (withholding and FATCA) purposes.

sources.title: Business Email Compromise: The $43 Billion Scam (PSA I-050422-PSA)
sources.publisher: Federal Bureau of Investigation, Internet Crime Complaint Center
sources.supports: 241,206 business email compromise incidents and US$43.3 billion of exposed losses from June 2016 to December 2021; use secondary channels or two-factor authentication to verify requests to change account information.

sources.title: Flow of funds in M&A: what it is, who prepares it and what goes on it
sources.supports: The funds flow memo shows where every dollar goes, by bank account; buyer's counsel drafts it and the other side confirms; first draft about one week before closing and final version locked one to three business days before; payment schedule commonly due three business days before closing; call back every set of wire instructions on an independently obtained number and require two approvers above a set amount.

sources.title: Competition law and foreign investment review (Canadian public company M&A report)
sources.supports: Competition Act pre-merger notification when parties exceed $400 million and the target exceeds the transaction-size threshold ($93 million in 2024); a notifiable transaction cannot close until a 30-day waiting period expires, extended by a supplementary information request; advance ruling certificates usually within 14 to 21 days; Investment Canada Act review of up to 45 days, extendable by 30, and notifications that can be filed up to 30 days after closing.

sources.title: Pre-merger notification transaction-size threshold to remain at $93M in 2024
sources.supports: Advance notice is generally required when the target's Canadian assets or revenues exceed $93 million and the parties' combined Canadian assets or revenues exceed $400 million; the threshold stays at the prior year's level when not adjusted.

sources.title: Deals are taking longer to close
sources.supports: Signing to closing for deals over $2 billion averaged 191 days in 2018 to 2022, up 11%; about 40% of deals closed later than announced; regulatory issues and complex structures were the most common causes of delay.

sources.title: Wages, Insurance Lawyer (NOC 41101) near Toronto (ON)
sources.supports: NOC 41101 lawyers, Toronto region hourly wages: low $33.65, median $69.74, high $112.98 (reference period 2023-2024).

assumptions: Mix of closings: 30% fund subscriptions and 70% direct and co-investments, split 45% private equity, 25% infrastructure and private credit, 30% real estate. The infrastructure associate also stands in for private credit deals, whose associates sit in global credit.

The case starts when negotiated documents arrive (70%, from investment-legal-agreements) or when a committee decision arrives for a sponsor-led co-investment with largely fixed documents (30%). Negotiation of the agreements themselves is in investment-legal-agreements and, for fund partnership agreements, in fund-commitment.

The step graph cannot remember which path a case came from, so the branch after the set-up check (17% of all closings have no payment at closing) is drawn for every case; in practice only fund subscriptions take it.

The model manager signs as agent for each owning client account; two authorised signatories and a senior payment approval threshold are assumed from common practice because the model manager's signing and payment authorities are not public.
Outside law firm hours are not modelled as roles; they show as waits and in counsel's coordination time.
Regulatory filings are assumed on about 12% of direct closings, mainly real estate and infrastructure control deals in Canada; minority co-investments rarely file.
The initial capital call of a new fund commitment is handled in capital-call-processing; announcements are drafted and issued in media-stakeholder-relations from the facts counsel clears here.

tax_analyst, compliance_analyst, general_counsel, cio, cash_collateral_analyst and head_investment_operations are organisation file roles that the process map does not list for this process; they appear for short steps.

Loaded costs come from the organisation file (Job Bank Toronto wages deflated to 2021, variable pay and a 1.35 loading). Hands-on time of about 25 hours a closing across in-house roles is the author's estimate.
The simulated 90th percentile (about 40 days) is below the 60-day estimate because regulatory filings and long sponsor delays fall on fewer than one closing in ten.
